logline: Three high-school students with secret superhuman abilities navigate first love and danger as the classified histories of their spy parents begin to surface in this prestige superhero epic based on Kang Full's Naver webtoon.

bollymeter.basis: Baeksang Grand Prize winner, 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes, MyDramaList 9.0 across 55,000 users, and six Asia Contents Awards including Best VFX. The most complete Korean prestige series of 2023 by every measurable signal.

pull_quotes.text: In adapting his own webtoon, Kang Full has stitched together a rich canvas, each character fleshed out and given their moment to shine.

seasons.review_body: Moving arrived as the most expensive Korean television series ever made, and the investment shows in every department. Twenty episodes structured around three generations of government-enhanced operatives, with the first seven functioning almost as standalone character studies before the threads converge. Critics initially flagged a slow opening cadence; the SCMP midseason recap noted ambition visible even through the early kinks. By the finale, the consensus had shifted to superlatives: Rotten Tomatoes 100 percent, Baeksang Grand Prize, six Asia Contents Awards. The structural gamble, spending enormous screen time on the parents' Cold War backstory before the teenage leads take center stage, paid off because director Park In-je and writer Kang Full gave the older generation genuinely tragic arcs. Disney's foothold in Korea, previously uncertain, was substantially strengthened by this single series.

episode_reviews.title: Senior Year
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Three high school students with no knowledge of each other's abilities meet on their first day. The episode is deliberately light and ordinary, establishing Bong-seok, Hui-soo, and Jang-ju as real teenagers before the show asks anything extraordinary from them or the audience.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bong-seok briefly, involuntarily levitating in the stairwell and catching himself before anyone sees - the show's premise delivered as comedy before it becomes something heavier.

critic_note.text: In adapting his own webtoon, Kang Full has stitched together a rich canvas, each character fleshed out and given their moment to shine.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The parents' Cold War backstory lands fully, and the show reveals why it spent six episodes building toward this - the generation before the teenagers carried a cost the teenagers are now inheriting. This episode was the pivot point that converted initial patience into evangelical word-of-mouth.
episode_reviews.the_moment: A flashback sequence that makes everything in episode one retroactively devastating - the structural payoff the show's slow opening was earning.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 14
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The action sequences that critics described as the best in Korean television history arrive here, with VFX that won the show six Asia Contents Awards. The episode is spectacular without losing the emotional grounding the first half built - the rare action climax that means something because the people in it do.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jang-ju's full-power sequence - the moment Moving crossed from prestige drama into something the genre rarely achieves.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 20
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale closes three generations of sacrifice with an ending that is earned rather than resolved - the characters arrive somewhere, but the show does not pretend the cost was small. Variety called Moving the next breakout hit from Asia after Squid Game; the finale is the evidence.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bong-seok running - and the audience understanding what that image now contains after twenty episodes.
